gloss: nagging; fault-finding; forever telling people off

definitions.explanation: Describes a person who comments critically on every little thing, or an atmosphere full of such complaints. Almost always negative, suggesting the criticism is more frequent than the situation deserves.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{口|くち}やかましい。
{口|くち}やかましい{上司|じょうし}に{疲|つか}れてしまった。
examples.english: I've grown tired of my fault-finding boss.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}の{目|め}が{口|くち}やかましくて、{夜遅|よるおそ}くに{洗濯|せんたく}もできない。
examples.english: The neighbors are so quick to complain that I can't even do laundry late at night.

notes:
Composed of {口|くち} (mouth) + やかましい (noisy, fussy). The complaint is verbal, so it applies to people and to the social pressure they create, not to loud sounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口|くち}やかましい{人|ひと}: a nagging person
- {口|くち}やかましく{言|い}う: to go on and on about something
- {口|くち}やかましい{世間|せけん}: a censorious public

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口|くち}うるさい: nagging — the more common everyday equivalent, essentially interchangeable
- やかましい: noisy; fussy — covers actual noise as well as fussiness
- {細|こま}かい: picky about details — can be neutral or even praise, unlike {口|くち}やかましい
